gaps.sentence: On the way to Rome we stopped ___ some photos.
gaps.hint: stop in order to do sth
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do; stop doing = finish doing. Here they paused to take photos.

gaps.sentence: The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: The rules don't ___ visitors to touch the paintings.
gaps.explanation: allow + object + to-infinitive: allow visitors to touch. (let + bare: let visitors touch.)

gaps.sentence: He apologised for ___ so rude to the waiter.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for being' — 'for' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: He was made ___ for the damage to the rental car.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, 'be made to do' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: We stopped at a village ___ some lunch.
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do something: stopped to have lunch.
